question: Did the genuine required-addition silently-SAFE gap already exist in the original direction-aware FORWARD implementation, before the later removal-detection fix?

commit_history.subject: feat: add profile-aware forward optional fields
commit_history.role: original direction-aware FORWARD/FULL implementation; first code state containing the gap

commit_history.subject: fix: evaluate removals in forward mode
fix: preserve required additions in forward mode

original_code_evidence.mechanical_diagnosis: The original implementation forwarded reversedDiff.requiredAdded() but never evaluated diff.requiredAdded(). A genuine base-to-candidate required addition therefore had no required-addition rule path in FORWARD. It was also iterated only as a field addition, so an open consumer resolved it through the optional-addition SAFE path.
original_code_evidence.blame_result: git blame e19aa13 -L 75,126 attributes the complete evaluateForward implementation to e19aa13d.

original_test_evidence.interpretation: The original direction-aware commit explicitly encoded the defective silent-PASS behavior before commit 18f0f04 existed.

reconstructed_test_run.change_to_test_only: Replaced the original PASS assertion with an assertion that breakingChanges() equals ["[FORWARD] Required field added: added"]. Production code was unchanged.
reconstructed_test_run.failure_excerpt: expected: <[[FORWARD] Required field added: added]> but was: <[]>
reconstructed_test_run.meaning: The gap is reproduced at e19aa13d itself and therefore was not introduced by the later removal-detection fix 18f0f04.
